Nothing stopped matching -- rombuild reports 106/106 exact with this TU in place. MEASURED with tools/tiers.py, the absorbing TU passes real_name, no_raw_offset, no_unk_field and no_codegen_trick, and fails EXACTLY ONE criterion, no_mangled_refs. The TU spells FIVE distinct external mangled symbols. MEASURED, FOUR of them are what tiers.MANGLED_REF (^_Z[0-9NK]) actually matches, and those four are what fails the criterion: (1) _ZN7fBase_cnwEj -- fBase_c::operator new, the allocation the ROM's Spawn performs; (2) _ZN10dBgActor_cC2Ev -- the base subobject construction Spawn does by hand; (3) _ZN10dBgW_KcMbg7SetFileEP8KCL_FileRK9Matrix4x35Fix12IiEsR10CLPS_Block; and (4) _ZN10dBgActor_c21IsClsnInRangeOnScreenE5Fix12IiES1_ -- one extern declaration plus two calls, both inside Behavior(). Seam (4) was omitted from the earlier wording of this row, which said "four" while naming a different four; this wording names all five. The fifth spelled symbol, _ZTV20daObjCannonShutter_c, is the hand-written vptr store beside _ZN10dBgActor_cC2Ev. It is mangled for the same ABI reason but does NOT trip no_mangled_refs, because ^_Z[0-9NK] never matches _ZT. Seam (3) is wall 6az: its by-value Fix12<int> is a constructor-less aggregate, so the member-call spelling emitted InitResources at 0xb8 against the cartridge's 0xac -- 12 bytes that overflowed the licensed range end and, because ov002 is the overlay every later overlay loads behind, dropped module fidelity to 20/106. Byte-match is goal 1; the mangled spellings stay.
